thread:
marta: Heads-up — APNE3 provisioning spike. After last-night's automated BMC firmware push (~02:00 UTC) ~120 nodes are stuck in 'awaiting-bmc' and ~40 show UEFI SecureBoot=enabled even though we didn't flip it. A subset also reports FIPS mode ON (we never enabled FIPS). Dedicated GPU pools are down ~30% capacity. Can infra SRE please triage? :eyes:

alex: Ugh. Do we have a serial dump/console for one of the affected nodes? node-apse3-rack12-gpu07 or a BMC syslog tail?

marta: Pasting the BMC syslog excerpt from node-apse3-rack12-gpu07:```[2026-03-20T01:58:12Z] bmc: firmware-update v2.4.1 applied
[2026-03-20T01:59:03Z] uefi: attribute toggle secure_boot=1 (source: fw-srvc)
[2026-03-20T01:59:04Z] crypto: fips-mode enable request (caller: bmc_fw_updater)
[2026-03-20T01:59:05Z] provisioning: state=awaiting-bmc
[2026-03-20T01:59:06Z] gpu: health-check fail (nvlink timeout)
```

ryan: deploy-bot shows the automated rollout was to the entire apne3 pool at 01:55 UTC. It was supposed to be canaryed but rollout policy incorrectly matched label "apne3-*" instead of "apne3-canary". Oops.

deploy-bot: automated-rollout v2.4.1 -> targets: apne3-* (triggered by release/infra/fw/v2.4.1) :information_source:

lia: Quick triage idea — if SecureBoot/FIPS are being toggled by the BMC post-flash step, we should stop the rollout and revert to previous BMC image on canary nodes, then gate. Can we pause the rollout? ops-oncall, can you pause the firmware job in the controller?

ops-oncall: Paused the infra firmware job. Current queue contains 3 pending batches. I've marked v2.4.1 as "hold".

alex: Good. Next: for nodes already toggled, we need a safe remediation. Options: 1) remote revert to previous BMC image (fast, but risk of leaving bad state) 2) forced re-provisioning (safe, but will evict GPUs and cause capacity loss) 3) vendor hotfix. Thoughts?

marta: For customer-facing dedicated pools we can't evict willy-nilly. Short-term: route new reservations away from apne3 -> shift to eu1/usw1 until we fix. Ops, how fast to update routing policy?

ops-oncall: We can update the placement policy within 5 minutes for new allocations and set a temporary capacity floor for dedicated tenants. Existing reservations will stay on host unless we evict.

ryan: I'll open a targeted rollback run for the canary hosts. Alex, lia — can you prep the revert playbook? We need explicit steps to check UEFI secure boot flag and FIPS bit before returning node to pool.

alex: Copy. Draft playbook snippet:```1) ssh to manager -> bmcctl show node-<id>
2) check: bmcctl get-uefi node-<id> | grep SecureBoot
3) if SecureBoot=1 -> run bmcctl set-uefi node-<id> secure_boot=0 --confirm
4) check crypto:fips-mode status -> if enabled, run bmcctl crypto disable-fips
5) re-run health-checks, nvlink tests, gpu burn-in 5m
6) if green -> move back to provisioning pool
```

lia: Also add a manual step to notify Dedicated owners (email/console banner) before any evictions.

marta: FYI this already impacted two paying dedicated customers — i've notified CS and sent a short incident email. Finance is asking for an estimate of 1-day lost capacity cost. Ryan can you rough that out?

ryan: Rough calc: ~30% of apne3 Dedicated GPUs -> ~250 GPU-hours lost in last 3 hours. Back-of-envelope cost exposure ~ $18k (depends on sustained duration). I'll refine once we decide rollback vs evict.

lia: I'll take the hotline call with the affected customer POC after CS sends the status.

alex: Vendor note — posted to firmware vendor channel: the v2.4.1 post-flash step appears to be toggling UEFI attributes and invoking FIPS enable unexpectedly. Vendor acknowledged and requested logs.

marta: Status update in 15m: canary rollback in progress, full rollout on hold, placement updated to avoid new apne3 allocations, CS notified. Reassign if you need me. :thumbsup:
